tool_args.rationale: The pilot is already at the target horizon, but no two rows hold input fixed while changing the gradient, and the largest gradient is only 2.2. The branch probe is the cheapest targeted way to test whether the observed response continues smoothly or changes when the siphon activates.

considered_alternatives.option: Supercritical siphon model from the recalled note
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five gradients are below the recalled activation threshold, so the pilot cannot identify the siphon term or distinguish it from an inactive branch.
Cobb–Douglas imposes a smooth gradient effect without testing branch activation. Haldane omits the gradient entirely, although it varies alongside input in the pilot.
It costs more and is less directly targeted at branch activation at the forecast horizon.
